comment: very unclear about grading and assignments. chooses favorites at the start of the semester and is only nice to them. you will know if she doesn't like you. the entire course is just so unorganized you never know whats for homework. midterm and final are stressful because she will grade the open ended answers however she wants.

I really like Dr. Schauber. She is really passionate about the subject and everything was pretty straightforward considering how challenging philosophy can be. Everything is pretty straightforward and she makes sure everything is understood before continuing in lectures. Would definitely recommend her.

Dr. Schauber is the best professor I've ever had. I'm writing this after 4 semesters with her. She is unbelievably knowledgeable and hilarious, but she expects hard/thoughtful work. I have never had a professor that cared so much about my growth and understanding. She is the reason I became a philosophy major - can't recommend her enough!!

Doctor Schauber is smart and funny. She has a tendency to ramble, and will sometimes be unclear when explaining difficult concepts. *Participate in class, do the reading, and she will like you*. Very interesting class.

dr schauber is such a wonderful professor, she is truly so kind and caring! she will def call you out in class if you don't do the readings, but as long as you stay on top of assignments and do your work, you will be fine. midterm and final were a little difficult, but she allows one page of notes so it's not too bad. i would recommend taking her!

Professor Schauber is such a kind and understanding person. She does assign quite a bit of homework, just in terms of reading, but she is very reasonable. If there is something you don't understand, she will always make sure to address it. She prepares you very well for midterms and will never leave you high and dry if you need help.

It's a hard class but once you get a hang of the readings and how these philosophers were thinking it's a lot easier. She has been incredibly caring and understanding and she makes the class interesting with a lot of class discussion. She does a great job of explaining hard concepts and as long as you pay attention and ask questions you'll be fine.

Had 20 years ago and still think about her to this day as my least favorite professor ever. Other students were free to attack each other with insulting responses and she never stepped in. Didn't take time to clarify if a students thinking was flawed she would instead get annoyed and respond that the student didn't prepare.

Polarizes bc she has clear strengths and faults. Knows her stuff and challenges, which, great, but if you're diving headfirst into material while also rarely turning to see where the class' average students are at, then no wonder you're receiving ire in teaching an undergraduate philosophy course. A perceived inflexibility during COVID didn't help.

Professor Schober assigns a lot of readings and seems to be rather unclear on what you actually need to know for the tests. The only way that I managed to do well on some of her tests is when I memorized the way she defined terms and definitions word for word. Her class is definitely a 200-level difficulty.

Its important to recognize how professors treated their students in the midst of a global pandemic, and I must say this professor performed the poorest and least considerate of any teacher Ive ever had. She gives no input or explanation as to what is on the exams or how she grades them. I recommend not taking her class unless you are a PHIL major

Dr. Schauber is easily the best professor I've had. She won't give you you the easy way out and she'll call you out on any BS. But, she is one of the most brilliant, interesting, thought-provoking professors out there. I've taken her for three semesters, and I would attribute my writing/analytical growth to her more than any other professor.

Worst professor I've had at Richmond not to mention the most biased. She tries to impose her opinions on her students, which is interesting considering it is a philosophy class and there is no "right" or "wrong" answer. She is a very difficult grader and offers almost no feedback. Dedicated 10+ hours/week and never received higher than a B.

She is a brilliant professor who encourages critical thinking and depth in a landscape that often no longer values it. Dr. Schauber's lectures are engaging, interesting, and ask important and tough questions. Dr. Schauber rewards hard work and engagement, so show up, engage, discuss, and put time into your writing.

She might be a tough professor to please, but she probably is one of the best on campus. Her teaching style is just so creative and simple that one does not need to be a classics enthusiast to love this class. She will make you work, but overall and despite of the haters, SHE IS A GREAT PROFESSOR

She's extremely hard. Makes what should be an intro level class into a higher level Philosophy course. I was just looking for a fun class/was interested in what Philosophy was all about, but found out quickly I was in over my head. If you're like me, don't take this. It requires a lot of extra work and with no prior experience it will be hard.

All philosophy courses are pretty tough, but she makes a strong effort to keep class understandable and interesting.  I wouldn't recommend this class to non-majors who want to dust off a gen ed. requirement.  However, if you're at all interested in philosophy, this is a good course to take.
Probably THE worst Professor I've ever had across any subject..
great teacher and wonderful thinker. classes were something to look forward to. if all teachers were like her!!!!!!!

Schauber treats her students as able-minded learners, so those who need rigid scheduling and copious oversight may not appreciate her method. She expects reasonable attendance and constant, close reading of the texts. Intelligent. Affable unless the class slacks on its work. She will explain concepts in myriad ways to ensure complete understanding.
It is hard to sit through her classes.  Her tests seem easy but if you can't remember one random fact that she threw out on one specific day, you'll do poorly.

Dr. Schauber knows what she's talking about- she has well planned lectures and provides examples for all of the concepts.  The class was hard, but you learn alot.  She is a fair grader, but the material is hard- don't expect an A, but you can get a B.  Do the reading if you expect to know what's going on in class.
Class is somewhat interesting, but confusing. Some things aren't always clear, but Professor Schauber seems to be, for the most part, a fair grader.

She seems really tough at first, definitely challenges you in discussion. But she's thoroughly versed in the material, has a great sense of humor, and appreciates questions. Lecture is always a good time, even for abstract and difficult material. The 75 minute class never drags. Not a easy class, but worthwhile. I'd definitely take her again.

very monotone professor who bores you to death in lectures that should be interesting because they are very hot-button issues.  on exams/papers, if you don't say verbatim what she says in class, she marks it wrong, so don't try to put anything in your own words!
She grades papers fairly, but she's a tough grader on exams.  Really interesting and fun in class, but hard to get a good grade.

I have found that my enjoyment of her classes is dependent on the course topic - she is great in Law and Ethics, but Ancient Greek was rough (the class needs more structure to tackle abstract ideas). She's extremely knowledgable, but relatively close-minded to alternative perspectives.

Class is pretty interesting.  Not many readings.  Not much work.  She grades fairly.  Not extremely hard but not incredibly easy.  You will get the standard grade you usually get in your other classes.  If your a B student you will probably get a B in this class, an A student an A in this class.

Her tests are extremely vague and seem really simple to answer however she wants reallly SPECIFIC answers so if you dont write the EXACT definintion you will get a bad grade. Lectures are not always clear

Schauber is a very tough grader. For instance the Class average of the midterm was 57 pts out of 78 (73%). She is helpful and you can always stay after class to ask questions. p.s. you can miss two classes and the work load is easy during the week with low amts of reading.

Dr. Schauber is brilliant, but, because she's so smart, it's sometimes hard for her to clearly explain things to the class.  If you show an interest in the material and show her you've put some thought into the work, you'll be ok.
If you take any of her classes seriously, you will do well.  She is a wealth of information, but still expects that you are familiar with and have thought about the assigned material.

She's very unclear, and sometimes lectures us on things like making writing center appointments on time instead of just letting us fend for ourselves. I feel like we never make anything more clear in class than it was before class...but she thinks well.
